candidates.title: 你吹一聲，我彈一下
candidates.prompt:
Using the supplied images for the TWO CHARACTER IDENTITIES and warm detailed hand-painted anime illustration style, REDRAW as a completely new SOUND-AND-MUSIC story scene for Taiwan middle-school Unit 3.3 "Characteristics of sound". Preserve: Xiaokui, brown eyes, brown DOUBLE BUN hair with natural bangs and loose wisps, ivory hoodie, dark/brown backpack straps if visible; Grandpa, fluffy silver-white hair, round thin glasses, absolutely CLEAN SHAVEN face, white coat over brown waistcoat and tie. Not another child hairstyle, no single ponytail, no moustache/beard. Natural faces and hands. Both full heads and essential instruments comfortably inside frame with 6% margin. Warm school MUSIC CORNER, wooden table, sunlight through a window, soft greenery, books and instrument shelves, not a lab bench full of glassware. Wide landscape 16:9, a single cinematic storybook scene, not collage, not infographic.
CRUCIAL USER CORRECTION: This must instantly read as PEOPLE MAKING, LISTENING TO, AND COMPARING AUDIBLE SOUNDS, not a physics wave laboratory. The visible physical actions, expressive listening and musical sound sources are the narrative. STRICTLY NO tablets, monitors, screens, oscilloscopes, waveform plots, graphs, sinusoidal curves, wave diagrams, control consoles/knobs, microphones, audio meters, dog/bat flashcards, technical posters, watery wave tanks, slinky springs, strings stretched across a science wall, floating sound ripples or magic sound ribbons. No displayed titles, words, letters, digits, speech bubbles, logos, watermarks, music notation, explanatory symbols. No giant science apparatus. Do not reuse meteorites, pencils, chemical vessels or measurement activities from the references.
Simple coherent instruments connect this sound story to later lessons: a compact WOODEN PLUCKED STRING SOUND BOX (one or two taut strings, clear bridges and a small tuning peg, small enough for a person's reach); and simple straight hollow open-ended sounding tubes, same material/bore but different lengths. Keep tubes straight with open cut mouths and no water or bent plumbing; if played, lips form a narrow air jet across an OPEN rim, NOT sealing the pipe like a straw. These connect string length/tension and air-column pitch. The story can continue to loud/soft, high/low, different timbres, hearing and describing sound levels; DO NOT cram all those concepts into props. No one in pain, no protective headphones, no industrial-noise scene. The scene should be warm, curious and playful, with clearly plausible instrument use. This is a narrative illustration, not a quantitative experiment diagram.

A natural CALL-AND-RESPONSE between a plucked string and a wind pipe. Eye-level medium-wide three-quarter view. Xiaokui is on the LEFT gently plucking the compact tabletop string sound box in front of her, bright-eyed with concentration. Grandpa on the RIGHT has a simple straight bamboo-colored sounding pipe ready in his hands, held below mouth level, and is clearly LISTENING to her current note with a slight curious forward lean; he will take the next turn. The girl's hands and instrument are the main focal triangle, and both faces are clearly visible. Two spare straight pipes of different lengths rest neatly on the far-right edge of the table, not on a science apparatus rack. A relaxed classroom music corner behind them. Emphasize human exchange 'try mine, then yours' and audible listening; no graphs or screens anywhere. Broad balanced hero composition, warm inviting sunlight.
